title: HRW: Russia's Africa Corps Su-24 Airstrike Killed 8 Civilians in Kyrnia, Mopti Region
detail: Human Rights Watch published an investigation on July 31, 2026 documenting a June 15, 2026 airstrike on Kyrnia village (Mopti region) that killed 8 civilians, including at least three children. A Sukhoi Su-24, identified via Malian military sources, dropped at least two munitions on a market day: the first strike near the village chief's residence killed his wife and two children plus one more child; a second strike roughly 20m away on a cattle market killed four men, including three merchants. HRW's investigation — based on interviews with 19 people plus satellite imagery and video analysis — found that while roughly 100 fighters from an al-Qaeda-linked group (JNIM) were present in the area, they were concentrated at a mosque and shop about 150m from the actual impact sites, with no evidence of a military objective at the points struck. HRW senior Sahel researcher Ilaria Allegrozzi said: 'Russian government-controlled Africa Corps aircraft have killed civilians in a Malian village in seeming disregard for the laws of war.' HRW called on Mali's junta to independently investigate, saying authorities 'cannot hide behind laws-of-war violations committed by their Russian allies.'

title: Suspected ISSP Fighters Overrun Two Niger Military Bases — Dankassari (Dosso) and N'Guigmi (Diffa)
detail: Suspected Islamic State Sahel Province (ISSP) fighters overran a Nigerien Defence and Security Forces forward operating base at Dankassari, between Doutchi and Yaya in Dosso Region, on July 31, 2026, killing 21 soldiers. A same-window attack was reported at N'Guigmi in Diffa Region near Lake Chad, with casualty figures disputed across outlets: security-analyst sourcing (Zagazola Makama) cited 17 killed including an officer, while other reporting described a National Guard post attack around 9:30am with a toll of roughly 10 FAN soldiers plus 4 National Guard (14 total), followed by an ambush of responding reinforcements about 1km south. Combined toll across both incidents is reported as roughly 38 dead, though official Nigerien government confirmation of the full total was not obtained. Group attribution is itself disputed: Niger's state news agency loosely attributed the attacks to 'Boko Haram,' while security-analyst reporting frames them under ISSP/Islamic State Sahel Province — related but distinct actors. Cumulative ACLED-tracked toll since Niger's July 2023 coup stands at 5,828 killed in terrorism-related violence, including 2,000+ security forces.
